title: What Happens When You Open a URL

scenes.line1: What happens when you open a URL?
scenes.say: Ever wondered what your browser does when you hit enter on a web address? Let’s break it down step by step.

First, your browser finds the server’s address using DNS. Then it opens a connection with TCP, secures it with TLS, and sends an HTTP request. Usually, a load balancer routes your request to a backend server, which sends back the data for your browser to render.

scenes.title: curl to a web app
scenes.say: Here’s what happens behind the scenes when you use a tool like curl. You can see DNS, TCP, TLS, the HTTP request, and the server’s response—all in action.

scenes.question: Is the load balancer always skipped?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it’s not part of the flow.
scenes.right: No, most requests hit a load balancer before reaching the backend.
scenes.say: Here’s a common interview trap: is the load balancer always skipped? Actually, most requests go through it before hitting the backend server.
